{{Short description|Canadian applied mathematician and computational neuroscientist}}
{{Use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=January 2021}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=January 2021}}
'''Sue Ann Campbell''' is a Canadian [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[Computational neuroscience|computational neuroscientist]] known for her work on [[dynamical system]]s, [[delay differential equation]]s, and their applications in modeling [[neural network]]s, [[population dynamics]], and [[Balance (ability)|balance]]. She is a professor of applied mathematics at the [[University of Waterloo]], former chair of the Department of Applied Mathematics,{{r|chair}} associate dean for research and international in the university's Faculty of Mathematics,{{r|ad}} and president of the Canadian Applied and Industrial Mathematical Society.

==Education and career==
Campbell has a bachelor's degree in mathematics (B.Math.) from the University of Waterloo, earned in 1986.{{r|ctn}} She completed her Ph.D. in 1991 at [[Cornell University]]. Her dissertation, ''The Effects of Symmetry on the Dynamics of Low-Dimensional Modal Interactions'', was supervised by [[Philip Holmes]].{{r|mg}}

She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Montreal]] before taking an assistant professor position at [[Concordia University]]. She returned to the University of Waterloo as an assistant professor in 1994.{{r|x}}

She was elected as president of the Canadian Applied and Industrial Mathematical Society in 2021, for a term beginning in 2023.{{r|pres}}

==Recognition==
Campbell was the 2005 winner of the Arthur Beaumont Distinguished Service Award of the Canadian Applied and Industrial Mathematics Society.{{r|beaumont}}
